cls: Prokinetic - dopamine D2 antagonist with acetylcholinesterase inhibition
pharm: Blocks dopamine D2 receptors and inhibits acetylcholinesterase, increasing acetylcholine to enhance gastric motility and accelerate gastric emptying; the D2 blockade also gives an antiemetic effect
quick: 50 mg three times daily before meals
Take before food (about 15-30 min before meals)
Avoid - excreted in milk in animals
No specific interaction; avoid if it worsens symptoms
Symptom response; prolactin if long-term; extrapyramidal symptoms
summary: Itopride is an oral prokinetic agent used for functional (non-ulcer) dyspepsia and symptoms such as bloating, early satiety, upper abdominal discomfort, nausea and vomiting. It acts both as a dopamine D2-receptor antagonist and as an acetylcholinesterase inhibitor, increasing gastric acetylcholine to enhance motility and gastric emptying. The usual adult dose is 50 mg three times daily before meals. Itopride is NOT approved by the US FDA; it is marketed in India, Japan and parts of Europe and Asia. Its quaternary structure limits central penetration, so extrapyramidal effects and hyperprolactinaemia are less frequent than with metoclopramide.
indications: Gastrointestinal symptoms of bloating, early satiety, upper abdominal pain/discomfort, anorexia, nausea and vomiting due to reduced gastric motility

dosage.n: Reduce dose or stop once symptoms resolve; reassess if no benefit
Monitor for cholinergic and extrapyramidal effects

admin: Take orally before meals to optimise the prokinetic effect
Use for the shortest period needed to control symptoms and reassess response
Discontinue if no symptomatic benefit is obtained
moa: Itopride has a dual mechanism: it antagonises dopamine D2 receptors and inhibits acetylcholinesterase. D2 blockade removes dopaminergic inhibition of gastrointestinal motility and provides a central/peripheral antiemetic effect, while acetylcholinesterase inhibition increases the local concentration of acetylcholine. The net result is enhanced gastric and duodenal contractility and accelerated gastric emptying. Itopride is metabolised mainly by flavin-containing monooxygenase (FMO3) rather than the cytochrome P450 system, giving it a low potential for CYP-mediated drug interactions, and its structure limits passage across the blood-brain barrier.

absolute: Conditions in which increased gastrointestinal motility is harmful, such as gastrointestinal haemorrhage, mechanical obstruction or perforation
monitor: Serum prolactin if galactorrhoea/gynaecomastia or with prolonged use

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established. Avoid use during pregnancy unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: Itopride is excreted in the milk of lactating animals; safety in breastfeeding is not established. Avoid use, or discontinue breastfeeding, during therapy.
renal: Limited data are available. Use with caution in renal impairment and monitor for accumulation and adverse effects.
hepatic: Limited data are available. Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Anticholinergic agents - antagonise the prokinetic effect of itopride
moderate: Other prokinetics or dopamine antagonists - additive effects/extrapyramidal risk
Drugs whose absorption depends on gastric emptying rate - altered absorption
minor: Low potential for CYP450-mediated interactions (metabolised mainly by FMO3)
interactions.food: Take before meals; food does not markedly impair efficacy when timed correctly

monitoring: Symptomatic response and need for continued therapy
Serum prolactin if symptoms suggest hyperprolactinaemia or with prolonged use
Liver function if jaundice or systemic symptoms develop
counsel: Take the tablet before meals as directed
Report breast tenderness, milky discharge or, in men, breast enlargement
Report any involuntary movements, tremor or muscle stiffness
Tell your doctor if symptoms do not improve so treatment can be reviewed
Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding unless advised by your doctor
pk: Prokinetic effect within about 30-60 minutes of an oral dose
Store at controlled room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: NOT FDA-approved; data are from SmPC/regional labels (India, Japan, EU) and BNF-type references
Dual action: D2 antagonism plus acetylcholinesterase inhibition
Metabolised mainly by FMO3, so low CYP-mediated interaction potential
Quaternary structure limits CNS entry - fewer extrapyramidal/prolactin effects than metoclopramide
Contraindicated where increased GI motility is harmful (bleeding, obstruction, perforation)
Take before meals and use for the shortest effective period
missed: If you miss a dose, take it before your next meal as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for the next dose - in that case skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses together.
overdose: Experience with overdose is limited. Expected effects relate to excess cholinergic activity (abdominal cramps, diarrhoea, salivation) and possible extrapyramidal symptoms. Management is supportive and symptomatic; anticholinergics may be used for extrapyramidal reactions.
